newsitem.title: INDIA: India clears private investment rules for highways.
newsitem.headline: India clears private investment rules for highways.

text.p: The Indian cabinet on Wednesday approved a new policy for the development of national highways, including guidelines for private investments in the sector, Surface Transport Minister T.G. Venkatraman said.
He told a news conference the cabinet had approved new measures for land acquisition, simplification of environmental clearances, procedures for financial approvals and levy of tolls.
"These are major steps to expedite highway development," Venkatraman said.
Venkatraman also announced the government had issued an ordinance to set up an independent authority which would decide tariffs for major ports.
"The authority will exercise all the powers of the government in fixing and revising port tariff. It will function independently of government," he said.
Venkatraman said its procedures would be transparent and it would consult with developers, port authorities and users to ensure that the tariff fixed was balanced.
According to the approved guidelines for private investments in road projects, investors will be allowed to revise the toll fee every year, linked to the wholesale price index.
Investors who subscribed to shares or debentures issued by a firm solely to develop and operate an infrastructure facility, will be eligible for tax deductions.
He said the government proposed to set up a separate fund to finance road development for which money would be made available through levying tolls on national highways.
